sentences.text: Normanniasaurus genceyi is the sole species of a basal titanosaurian, a type of large sauropod dinosaur.
This animal shares several primitive traits with slightly younger relatives like Epachthosaurus and Andesaurus.

The known fossil material includes a partial skeleton with presacral vertebrae fragments, a partial sacrum, anterior and middle caudal vertebrae, a right scapula, ilia and ischia fragments, and parts of the femur and fibula.
The genus was first described and named by Jean Le Loeuff, Suravech Suteethorn, and Eric Buffetaut in 2013.
The specific name genceyi honors Pierre Gencey, who discovered the remains in July 1990.
The holotype specimens, which are the specific fossils the species is based on, are housed at the Museum d'histoire naturelle du Havre.
Normanniasaurus lived during the middle of the Cretaceous period, approximately 113 to 107 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
Its time range corresponds to the Albian stage, from 110.1 to 106.3 million years ago.
Scientists consider the late Early Cretaceous radiation of basal Titanosauria in South America, Europe, and Africa to be an unusual pattern.
